title: Woe to the one who mocks and belittles people.
subtitle: Slander by word and by gesture
then: Every Arab knew this character and thought it ugly, Maududi says. Ibn Kathir explains one slanders by speech, the other by action: {trap}he finds fault with people and belittles them{/trap}. Mujahid said humazah is with the hand and eye, lumazah {trap}with the tongue{/trap}.
now: The eye-roll when a colleague speaks in a meeting. The screenshot shared with a laughing emoji. The impression of your aunt's accent at dinner. {trap}None of it feels like a big sin.{/trap} The surah opens with woe for exactly this.
old: It is just a joke. Everyone does it.
new: An eye-roll or a joke at someone's expense is serious enough to open a surah with woe.
try: Today, when you feel the urge to mock someone, even silently, say something kind about them instead.

title: He gathers money and counts it again and again.
subtitle: Wealth that fills the whole day
then: Ibn Kathir says he {trap}piles some of it on top of the rest and counts it up{/trap}. Muhammad bin Ka'b said: his wealth occupies his day, going from this to that, and {trap}at night he sleeps like a corpse{/trap}.
now: Checking the banking app at red lights. Refreshing the investment chart before bed. Calculating what everyone else earns. {idea}The verse puts the counter right after the mocker{/idea}: looking down on people often grows from counting what you have.
old: Keeping track of my money is just being careful.
new: When counting money fills my day, it starts to fill my heart and shape how I see people.
try: Do not check your bank balance or investments today. Notice how often you want to.

title: He thinks his money will keep him alive forever.
subtitle: The quiet belief behind hoarding
then: Ibn Kathir says {trap}he thinks gathering wealth will make him last forever in this worldly life{/trap}. Nobody says it out loud. Maududi notes such people often seem to thrive here, which is why {idea}the Hereafter becomes necessary{/idea}.
now: The pension planner says you are set until 95. The insurance covers every case. It feels like {trap}nothing can touch you now{/trap}. Then a scan result arrives that no money can reverse. The verse names the belief behind the spreadsheet.
old: If I save enough, I will be safe from whatever comes.
new: Money can soften life, but it cannot extend it by a single breath.
try: Write down one thing money cannot protect you from. Ask Allah for protection from it.

title: No. He will be thrown into the Crusher.
subtitle: The end of the one who belittled others

row.title: No!
sub: it is not as he claims

then: Ibn Kathir says {idea}But no!{/idea} means the matter is not as he claims. Al-Hutamah is one of the names of the Fire, called so {trap}because it crushes whoever is in it{/trap}. The one who broke people down meets a name that matches.
now: You have watched someone crush another person with a comment, and walk away smiling. Maybe you have done it. {idea}The verse says the matter is not as they think.{/idea} Turn it on yourself: whose spirit have you crushed lately?
old: People who put others down usually get away with it.
new: Nobody gets away with crushing people. Allah answers with a single word: no.
try: Think of one person you made feel small. Apologise to them today, or make dua for them.

title: Do you know what the Crusher is?
subtitle: A question before the description
then: As in Al-Qari'ah, Allah pauses with a question before describing the Fire. Maududi says the surah is built so that {idea}the listener reaches the conclusion himself{/idea}: a man with this character {trap}deserves this end{/trap}.
now: You have read many warnings and they have slid off. This question puts a hand on your shoulder. {idea}Stop. Do you actually know?{/idea} The answer that follows is not for curiosity, it is for change.
old: I know what Hell is. I do not need it explained.
new: Allah's question tells me I do not fully know, and that it matters that I learn.
try: Pause after reading this card and ask Allah to keep your tongue and eyes from belittling anyone.

title: It is Allah's own fire, kept burning.
subtitle: A fire with His name on it
then: This is the answer to the question. The fire is named as {trap}the fire of Allah{/trap}, kindled and kept alight. Ibn Kathir places it as the explanation of Al-Hutamah, the end of {idea}the one who gathered wealth and belittled people{/idea}.
now: People who mock others often think nobody important is watching. The verse attaches Allah's own name to the answer. {idea}Belittling His servants is not a small matter to Him.{/idea} It also means His justice for the belittled is personal.
old: Mocking people is a small social thing, not something Allah cares about.
new: Allah takes the dignity of His servants personally, including the ones I find easy to mock.
try: Defend someone today who is being mocked, even with one sentence.

title: It reaches all the way to the heart.
subtitle: Where the mockery began
then: Thabit Al-Bunani said it will reach them all the way to their hearts, and {trap}then he cried{/trap}. The mockery and the hoarding both began in the heart: {idea}contempt for people and love of wealth{/idea}.
now: The cruel joke starts long before you say it. It starts as a small feeling of being better than someone. {idea}That feeling is in your heart right now, or it is not.{/idea} The verse goes straight to the root.
old: What matters is what I say, not what I feel.
new: Contempt begins in the heart. That is where I need to clean first.
try: When you catch yourself feeling superior to someone today, make a quiet dua for them.

title: It will be closed over them.
subtitle: No way out once the door shuts
then: Ibn Kathir says this means {trap}covering{/trap}, as explained in Surat Al-Balad. Ibn Abbas said {trap}the gates will be shut upon them{/trap}. The man who thought nothing could close in on him is closed in.
now: Every closed door implies a time it was open. {reward}Right now the door of repentance is wide open{/reward} for anyone who mocked, hoarded, or looked down on others. That is what this verse is pointing to.
old: There is always time to change later.
new: One day the doors close. Today they are open, so today is when I walk through.
try: Make tawbah today for one specific time you belittled someone.

title: In long, stretched-out columns.
subtitle: The final image of the surah

key.label: What he built, what holds him

then: Atiyah Al-Awfi said {trap}pillars of iron{/trap}. As-Suddi said made of fire. Ibn Abbas said there will be columns over them. The surah ends on this image, the opposite of {idea}the towering wealth he piled up and counted{/idea}.
now: You see the towers people build: portfolios, follower counts, status. They look like they hold you up. {idea}This surah asks what you are building, and whether it will hold you up or hold you down.{/idea} It is not too late to build differently.
old: What I pile up here will hold me up.
new: What I build from contempt and greed becomes the thing that holds me down.
try: Give something you have been holding onto to someone who needs it more.
